mathematical_reason: ProofWiki Sigma-Algebra, Definition 1, explicitly requires X to lie in Σ, closure under complements relative to X, and closure under countable unions. A sigma-algebra differs from a topology and need not contain every subset of X. The empty set follows from closure under complements.
source_specific_context: Measure theory: family of subsets closed under relative complements and countable unions

mathematical_reason: ProofWiki Measure (Measure Theory), Definition 2, requires nonnegative extended-real values, zero on the empty set, and countable additivity over pairwise disjoint measurable sets. It does not require μ(X)=1, finite total measure, or a previously defined Lebesgue-Stieltjes integral.
source_specific_context: Measure theory: extended nonnegative countably additive set function on a sigma-algebra
